newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares rebound on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares rebound on bargain hunting.

text.p: Singapore's key share index rose 1.25 percent Monday, driven by bargain-hunting after nearly eight days of decline.
The Straits Times Industrials Index, which had lost 100 points since March 11, ended 25.92 points up at 2,094.40.
Dealers said renewed optimism over the local property market and a technical rebound in property counters like Wing Tai and Cycle & Carriage (C&C) boosted the index.
"It's just that most of these stocks are blue-chips and have dropped quite a bit over last week and now seems like a good time to pick them up," said a broker at a local institution.

Dealers said Wing Tai's 111 percent gain in interim profits to Singapore $91 million and C&C's 10 percent jump in 1996 profits to S$200.1 million sent the shares higher. Wing Tai ended S$0.24 up at S$4.28 while C&C rose S$0.50 to S$15.20.
Foreign tranches of banks like DBS, OUB and OCBC also rose.
Insurance company Great Eastern Life Assurance shed S$0.20 to end at S$21.20 after a 21.3 percent drop in 1996 profits.
Marine logistics compnay, Labroy Marine topped the actives with over 14 million shares, including the 10 million crossed at S$2.00 in the morning. The shares ended at S$2.03, up S$0.02.
